question: Let R be a point on a straight line PQ. Two Circles are drawn with diameters PR and PQ. Let A be any point on the circumference of the circle with diameter PQ. If PA meets the other circle at B, then:
solution:
**Given:**

R is a point on a straight line PQ.

Two circles are drawn with diameters PR and PQ.

A is any point on the circumference of the circle with diameter PQ.

PA meets the other circle at B.

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f7c84c9008c0b1f000bdfb77a84de42a77d073d63eb2a722f9b79186833bebc2.png] 

⇒ As A lies on the circumference of circle it makes a right angle with the diameter of circle, i.e., ∠PAQ = 90° 

⇒ Similarly, ∠PBR = 90°

As both lies on PQ line and makes 90° angle

In ∆PBR and ∆PAQ,

⇒ ∠P = ∠P (common)

⇒ ∠B = ∠A (right angle)

⇒ ∆PBR and ∆PAQ are similar triangles (By A-A property)

∴ BR ∥ AQ

⇒ BR/AQ = PR/PQ

⇒ There is no relation given between PR and PQ so, BR may not be equal to ½ AQ.

⇒ It will only be possible when R is the mid-point of line PQ.

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**
